title: A High-Performance Stochastic Simulated Bifurcation Ising Machine
problem: Simulated bifurcation Ising machines suffer from high energy consumption despite their benefits from massive parallelism in solving combinatorial optimization problems. Efficient hardware implementations are needed to make these machines practical.
motivation: Ising machines are promising solvers for combinatorial optimization problems, but energy efficiency must be improved for practical deployment.
method: The algorithm cuts energy use by replacing expensive multiply-and-accumulate operations (multiplying numbers and adding them together) with cheaper multiplexing and addition. It computes the math using signed stochastic integrators—circuits that use randomness to approximate sums rather than calculating precisely, which saves energy. The algorithm also restricts position values to just three states (called ternarizing) instead of keeping them as full-precision numbers, further reducing the data that hardware must process. Two interchangeable cell types—one with two stochastic integrators and another with one binary integrator plus one stochastic integrator—stack together to build the complete machine.
key_novelty: The key idea is combining randomness-based calculations (stochastic computing) with simulated bifurcation by designing the algorithm and hardware together, which reduces energy consumption and chip area.
contributions: Stochastic simulated bifurcation (sSB) algorithm converting MAC operations to multiplexing and addition
Hardware designs for two types of SB cells using signed stochastic integrators for efficient integration
SSBM implementations with 10.62% smaller area than state-of-the-art designs
Demonstration of stochastic computing efficiency for solving combinatorial optimization problems
primary_theme: Stochastic hardware accelerators for combinatorial optimization
